Use child_process spawn/execFile with an argument array (no shell string built from user input), a per-test timeout (for example 5 s, configurable) that kills the process, a build timeout (for example 15 s), and an output size cap. 8. Add a short README.md section: how to install, start the server, and run the runner check.

function spawnCommand(command: string, opts): Promise<SpawnOutcome> {
  const tokens = tokenize(command);
  if (tokens.length === 0) {
    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: "", stderr: "empty command", exitCode: null, timedOut: false });
  }
  const [cmd, ...args] = tokens;
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let stdout = "";
    let stderr = "";
    let exitCode: number | null = null;
    let timedOut = false;
    let settled = false;

    const child = spawn(cmd, args, {
      cwd: opts.cwd,
      env: process.env,
      stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
      detached: process.platform !== "win32",
    });

    const append = (target: "stdout" | "stderr", chunk: Buffer) => {
      const s = chunk.toString("utf8");
      if (target === "stdout") {
        const space = opts.maxOutputBytes - stdout.length;
        if (space > 0) stdout += s.slice(0, space);
      } else {
        const space = opts.maxOutputBytes - stderr.length;
        if (space > 0) stderr += s.slice(0, space);
      }
    };

    child.stdout?.on("data", (d) => append("stdout", d));
    child.stderr?.on("data", (d) => append("stderr", d));

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      timedOut = true;
      killProcessTree(child);
      finish();
    }, opts.timeoutMs);

    const finish = () => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ stdout, stderr, exitCode, timedOut });
    };

    child.once("error", (err) => {
      stderr += `\n[runner] failed to spawn '${cmd}': ${err.message}`;
      finish();
    });

    child.once("exit", (code) => {
      exitCode = code;
      finish();
    });

    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
    if (opts.input !== undefined) {
      child.stdin?.write(opts.input);
    }
    child.stdin?.end();
  });
}

function tokenize(command: string): string[] {
  const tokens: string[] = [];
  let current = "";
  let quote: "'" | '"' | null = null;
  for (let i = 0; i < command.length; i++) {
    const ch = command[i];
    if (quote) {
      if (ch === quote) quote = null;
      else current += ch;
    } else if (ch === '"' || ch === "'") {
      quote = ch;
    } else if (ch === "\\" && i + 1 < command.length) {
      current += command[i + 1];
      i += 1;
    } else if (/\s/.test(ch)) {
      if (current) { tokens.push(current); current = ""; }
    } else {
      current += ch;
    }
  }
  if (current) tokens.push(current);
  return tokens;
}

# HintLab

A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an
assignment; the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases in a
sandbox and (in later steps) delivers tiered hints.

This is **Step 01**: the Express + TypeScript server skeleton and the sandboxed
code runner. There is no Cline SDK agent or web UI yet.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22+ (verified on Node 24)
- Python 3 (`python3`) on PATH
- `gcc` on PATH (for the C assignment)

## Install

```sh
npm install
```

## Start the server

```sh
npm run dev      # watch mode
npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
```

The server listens on `http://localhost:3000` by default. Override with `PORT`:

```sh
PORT=4000 npm start
```

### Endpoints

| Method | Path              | Description                                            |
| ------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/health`     | Liveness check                                         |
| GET    | `/api/assignments`| List assignments (id, language, statement, starter code) |
| POST   | `/api/session`    | Run a submission. Body: `{ assignmentId, code? }`       |

`POST /api/session` returns `{ sessionId, testResults }`. If `code` is omitted,
the assignment's starter program is used.

```sh
curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/api/session \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list","code":"print(sum(map(int, input().split())))"}'
```

## Run the runner check

```sh
npm run test:runner
```

This runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starter programs and
asserts the exact expected pass/fail of every test, plus a correct solution for
